body.text: Why Donald Trump is taking credit for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia and US President Donald Trump is taking credit for the move.
Mr Huang resigned from Nvidia last week after it was revealed he had a series of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.
Despite security concerns for the California-based company, the US president repeatedly expressed his support for the CEO — even when some of his own party's representatives did not.
"I spoke to them [the board], let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC.
Olivia Shen, the director of the Strategic Technologies Program at the US Studies Centre, said the intervention from the president in a company's leadership was "telling".
"It feels like Jensen Huang is a protected species," she said.
"It is telling in the video from Nvidia about reinstating him, they specifically say they have had advice from highest levels of the US government.
"It doesn't get much higher than the US president himself."
A 'national treasure'
Mr Trump lauded Mr Huang's reinstatement as the "correct and proper decision" after Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones had previously ruled out rehiring Mr Huang.

"The Country needs Jensen's leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," he wrote on Truth Social, describing Mr Huang as a "national treasure".

"The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."
The president also called for Nvidia to continue its internal investigation into its compliance with US export controls.
His comments come as the company and its boss face a host of state and federal probes over intelligence, antitrust and accounting matters.
Mr Trump also shared a meme of Mr Huang superimposed over a photo taken of himself after an assassination attempt in 2024.
A red bra dangles from Mr Huang's hand in an apparent reference to the sex scandal.
"It was quite extraordinary making light of what is a complicated national security situation," Ms Shen said.
"He sees Jensen as someone that he sort of relates to in a way; that he is someone who can come back swinging."
Intervention raises flags
Mr Huang's comeback sent Nvidia's shares soaring 33 per cent, on track to add more than $900 billion in market value.
The news of Mr Huang's return helped Wall Street recover from last week's sharp sell-off.
On Friday, the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections as worries mounted about the AI trade.
"Mr Trump certainly sees that as a marker of success when it is up and America and his allies are profiting," Ms Shen said.
The president was asked whether the stock losses following Mr Huang's resignation had influenced his decision to intervene.
"Probably so," he said.
"But the bigger impact was the long term. He's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about."

Mr Trump's investment accounts have bought and sold Nvidia stock at least 103 times since he returned to the White House, with transactions worth up to $US97.5 million ($147 million), according to CNBC.
The US government also receives cuts of Nvidia's business with China, which the Cato Institute estimates has netted it about $US333 million.
Mr Trump has maintained a close friendship with Mr Huang since the start of his second term, frequently inviting the tech leader to White House meetings and on diplomatic trips to the UK and China.
Ms Shen said while it was clear Mr Trump considered Mr Huang's leadership valuable to Nvidia, the intervention raised some flags.
"I do think it is very much a personal intervention and the way it has been done is in line with many concerns Democrats have about corruption," she said.
"Mr Trump has surrounded himself with loyalists and Jensen fits that category — especially now.
"The president's measures to reinstate him makes me wonder: Is Jensen owing his position to the president and how will that impact him going forward?"
Concern in Congress
The president's vocal support of Mr Huang has not erased concerns of international interference among several members of both parties in Congress.

Senate Intelligence Committee chair Tom Cotton, a Republican, called on Congress to pass the Chip Security Act, which seeks to address legally exported advanced chips that are later diverted to China, where their sales are restricted.
The bill would require chipmakers to track the location of advanced AI processors and notify the government if they suspect chips have reached prohibited users.
For Nvidia, the measure could create new compliance costs and reporting obligations.
Democratic senator Elizabeth Warren said Nvidia's board still owed Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls.

"Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure Nvidia does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk," she said.
Mr Huang will testify before the ‌US Senate Banking Committee in a public hearing on December 3 as politicians probe allegations about his ties to Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy.

"The US government has blacklisted the company that Alice Huang worked for, and clearly has national security concerns about this company, but Jensen Huang gets to be reinstated with the full support of the president while investigations are ongoing," Ms Shen said.
"It doesn't make a lot of sense."
ABC/Reuters
